causes.text: Tesla rolled out a new round of price cuts on vehicles and its Full Self-Driving software across China, Europe and North America, lowering the cost of the Model 3 by around 14,000 yuan in China and signalling continued aggression in pricing to boost demand.

source_info.title: Tesla cuts prices in China, Germany and around globe

effects.text: Roughly a year later, BYD reduced the starting price of its budget Seagull electric car to 55,800 yuan and offered trade-in incentives, further intensifying China's EV price war and maintaining its value positioning.

source_info.title: China auto shares sink after BYD offers trade-in incentives

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2024-04-21, Tesla implemented fresh price cuts on its vehicles and FSD software across major markets, reducing the price gap between premium and budget EVs.
The sustained price aggression by Tesla kept competitive pressure high, prompting consumers to expect lower prices across the sector.
In response, on 2025-05-26 BYD trimmed the Seagull's starting price to 55,800 yuan and rolled out trade-in incentives, ensuring it remained competitively priced against Tesla and others.
On 2025-05-26, after the price cut announcement, BYD's shares plunged by approximately 8.6% as investors assessed the impact on profit margins.

rationale: Tesla's repeated global price cuts continued to set the tone for the EV market, forcing rivals to follow suit to maintain sales momentum. BYD's reactive pricing strategy of trimming the Seagull's price and offering trade-in incentives demonstrates its effort to defend market share amidst fierce competition.
counterfactual_analysis: If Tesla had not continued cutting prices, BYD might have maintained the Seagull's original pricing or offered smaller incentives, preserving margins.

adversarial_confounders.impact: BYD may have cut prices to clear excess inventory independent of Tesla's pricing decisions.

details.commentary: Tesla's aggressive round of price cuts in China, Europe and North America intensified price-based rivalry across the EV market. BYD's subsequent decision to lower the Seagull's price and add trade-in incentives shows how competitors are forced to respond to protect share, even at the risk of margin pressure.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Slowing demand and heightened price sensitivity in the EV market
details.commentary: Macroeconomic uncertainty and stretched household budgets made EV buyers more price-sensitive, especially in mass-market segments. These economic conditions amplified the impact of Tesla's cuts and pushed BYD to defend its value positioning with deeper discounts, feeding into a broader price war.
